attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation with 'so far' kept. The joke about the name is rhetoric, but the 'isn't working' part is a factual claim.

contract.note: Reading 'isn't working' as falling short of goals or release is the ordinary reading, given the WSJ delay reports two days earlier. A literal 'fails to run' reading would be stretched against the speaker.

evidence.note: Fortune, relaying the WSJ on 2025-05-16, inside the period: release delayed after engineers struggled to improve its capabilities.
WSJ passage, 2025-05-15: executives blame the team for failure to make progress on Behemoth. Unnamed sources, but a major outlet.
Meta's own April 5 disclosure: wins on some STEM benchmarks, but still training and not released. It does not say the model was meeting goals or on track, so the contradiction condition is not met.
July 2025 NYT report via Slashdot: release delayed due to poor internal performance. Published after the period, so it only confirms the earlier reports.

reviews.rationale: Credible reports from the period (WSJ via e1, e2) say Meta delayed Behemoth because its capabilities fell short and progress stalled. Meta's earlier benchmark claims are a company disclosure. They say the model was still training and do not show it on track. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own aside in his own post.

semantics.note: The factual aside 'never turned a profit' is pulled out correctly. The light-cone remark is rhetoric and is rightly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading (no annual net profit from 2015 to May 2025, based on credible press estimates) is ordinary and fair. The nonprofit years are flagged as ambiguous, but no source suggests profit then.

evidence.note: Salon, January 2025, before the post: OpenAI hasn't turned a profit, with about $5B in projected 2024 losses.
NYT via PYMNTS, Sept 2024: company documents project about a $5B loss for 2024. This is a projection, not a realized figure.
The Information via SiliconANGLE: 2022 loss of $540M, double the prior year's, which implies a loss in 2021 too.

reviews.rationale: Credible reports show net losses in 2021, 2022 and (projected) 2024, and no source reports a profitable year before May 2025. Figures for 2015-2020 and 2023 are missing, but the contract's support condition is met.
